title: Explicit ridge around a nonzero prior with a non-uniform penalty
description: The same four weighted points as the heteroscedastic case, but pulled toward a prior of (1, 1) with lambda = 2 and a diagonal penalty that penalizes the slope twice as hard as the intercept.
assumptions: The response is linear in x, with an intercept.
The prior of (1, 1) is a real belief about where the parameters should sit, not a placeholder.
Penalizing the slope twice as hard as the intercept reflects a real belief that the slope is the more suspect of the two.
limitations: The estimate is deliberately biased toward the prior. The analytic interval describes the spread of that biased estimate; it does not include the bias.
Lambda was declared, not chosen. Nothing here says it is the right lambda.
